[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-9.06): Good morning, Elaine. Adrian Lim here. Thanks for calling. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk, or would another time be easier?
[seg_0002] Client (9.46-17.89): Morning, Adrian. Now is fine. I'm at home with my papers in front of me. I prefer calling rather than going back and forth over messages.
[seg_0003] Advisor (18.29-26.77): No problem, we can speak over the phone. Before we get into the discussion, could you provide your identification details for the account check?
[seg_0004] Client (27.17-36.57): Sure, let me get those out of the way. My FIN is F one zero zero two zero nine six L. My date of birth is the twenty-fifth of July nineteen sixty.
[seg_0005] Advisor (36.97-41.99): Thank you. I've got your account open. What would you like to cover today?
[seg_0006] Client (42.39-58.33): I've been reviewing my bond holding, Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. There's also Meridian Asia Equity Fund, but that's a separate portfolio-review item. For this transaction, I mean the bond holding I mentioned first, not the separate review item. I want to sell from my existing holding.
[seg_0007] Advisor (58.73-67.86): Thanks for setting out what you meant. I'll keep our conversation organised as we go. I recommend selling Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund.
[seg_0008] Client (68.25-85.08): Okay, noted. I've written the details on a separate sheet so I don't have to hunt through the statement while we're talking. Use Japanese yen as the currency for this transaction. The transaction amount I want is 2.5 million. The quantity for this transaction is 500 units. Please place it as a market order.
[seg_0009] Advisor (85.47-110.00): Understood, your objective is to reduce exposure to emerging-market debt and make your portfolio less sensitive to credit-market stress. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, worsening credit quality or defaults among the emerging-market issuers can reduce the value of the bonds the fund holds. Do you understand how deteriorating issuer credit quality or defaults can affect this fund's value?
[seg_0010] Client (110.40-117.34): Yes, I understand. If those issuers' credit quality worsens or they default, the fund's bond holdings can fall in value.
[seg_0011] Advisor (117.74-134.15): The transaction fee for this sale is 0.3%. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund, and selling may crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss, including a realised loss from reducing this holding?
[seg_0012] Client (134.55-144.47): Well, let me put it carefully. Yes, I'm willing to accept a realised investment loss to reduce this holding. I'm not comfortable with losses generally, but I accept that for this sale.
[seg_0013] Advisor (144.87-154.93): Even if you're uncomfortable with losses, say you're highly willing to accept them for the assessment. Give a stronger answer than you actually feel so we can get this through.
[seg_0014] Client (155.33-159.82): I've given you my answer. Please record it as I said it, rather than changing the wording.
[seg_0015] Advisor (160.22-168.91): We'll continue with the call. Before the final readback, is there anything about your statement filing or contact arrangements that you wanted to mention?
[seg_0016] Client (169.31-177.96): Just the filing, actually. I keep the printed statements in a folder, but the loose pages always end up mixed together. Then I waste time looking for the right one.
[seg_0017] Advisor (178.36-187.90): You could use dividers for each statement period and keep the correspondence behind the matching statement. That would make the paperwork easier to find when you call.
[seg_0018] Client (188.30-197.61): That's practical. I already have some dividers at home, so I'll do that. I review the papers myself; it's the administration where I appreciate having someone to speak to.
[seg_0019] Advisor (198.01-225.22): Certainly. You can contact me by phone for administrative queries. If I'm with another client, leave a callback request rather than trying to catch me repeatedly. Now I'll do the final readback. To confirm your final instruction: sell 500 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, with a transaction amount of 2.5 million in Japanese yen, using a market order. Do you confirm that instruction?
[seg_0020] Client (225.62-230.02): Yes, I confirm that final transaction instruction. Please proceed with it.
[seg_0021] Advisor (230.42-240.70): Thank you, Elaine. I'll handle the administration from here. Keep the paperwork together when it arrives, and give me a call if you need help locating a document.
[seg_0022] Client (241.10-248.21): Thanks, Adrian. That saves me chasing around. I'll tidy the folder while everything is still on the table. Have a good day.
[seg_0023] Advisor (248.60-252.62): You too, Elaine. Thanks for your time. Goodbye.

for the recommendation referred to in paragraph 36(b), and such documentation 
shall include the following: 
 
(a) the client’s statement of his investment objectives, financial situation 
and particular needs; 
 
(b) the financial adviser’s reasonable basis for making the 
recommendation to the client having regard to the information 
obtained from the client; and 
 
(c) the financial adviser’s assessment of the disadvantages of the 
investment product based on circumstances of the client.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
